messages.content: You are L3 draft v1. User: "Explain how a blockchain works in exactly one short paragraph, non-technical, no bullet points."

A blockchain is like a shared digital notebook that many people can see and write in, but no one can erase or secretly change. Every time something happens—like a transaction—it’s written as a “block” of information and linked to the block before it, forming a long chain. Copies of this notebook are stored on many computers around the world, and they all compare notes to agree on what’s true. Because everyone checks each other and old pages can’t be altered without everyone noticing, blockchain makes it very hard to cheat or fake records.
